**Proposed mechanism:** Smoothened (HGNC:10743) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP2571); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP2571) —LEADS_TO→ Phenotypic abnormalities associated with Curry-Jones syndrome (HP:0012832); Indian hedgehog homolog (HGNC:5474) —DISRUPTS→ Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP2571); Hedgehog signaling pathway (WP2571) —LEADS_TO→ Phenotypic abnormalities associated with acrocapitofemoral dysplasia (HP:0002657). Gain-of-function mutations in SMO lead to aberrant activation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway, contributing to the phenotypes seen in Curry-Jones syndrome. Loss-of-function mutations in IHH also disrupt the Hedgehog signaling pathway, albeit through a different mechanism, leading to the phenotypes observed in acrocapitofemoral dysplasia. Both diseases converge on the dysregulation of the Hedgehog signaling pathway.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of mutations in SMO or IHH in patients diagnosed with the other disease, or the identification of a distinct molecular pathway that independently explains the phenotypes of both diseases without involvement of the Hedgehog pathway, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in SMO or IHH in the general population that do not segregate with either Curry-Jones syndrome or acrocapitofemoral dysplasia.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on the Hedgehog signaling pathway, despite different causal genes and functional consequences, could reveal therapeutic opportunities. Modulators of the Hedgehog pathway might be beneficial for both conditions, although careful consideration of the specific gene and mutation context would be crucial to avoid exacerbating phenotypes.
